lines: Felicis founder Aydin Senkut argues the best venture opportunities have shifted to capital-intensive areas like robotics, physical AI and AI infrastructure: 'trillion-dollar markets with billion-dollar contracts' that scale revenue fast but need years of capital and carry customer concentration.
His 'multitude of signal' rule calls for three or four independent indicators of durable demand and foundational IP before a high-conviction bet, rather than a single growth metric or hype.
Senkut says he never votes against a founder, preferring to steer pivots with objective data so founders feel safe disclosing problems early.
He spends 10-20% of operating time on 'exit engineering', mapping specific acquisition or secondary paths, which he says raises the odds of returns in illiquid markets.

He judges Felicis, now investing from a billion-dollar seed and Series A fund, by 'success density' (share of strong outcomes) rather than AUM, and favors hungry 'underdog' founders outside Silicon Valley.
podcast: Capital Allocators – Inside the Institutional Investment Industry
title: Chasing Demand in Early-Stage Venture at Felicis – Aydin Senkut (EP.526)
